messages:
amanda: Heads-up — after the kernel + driver rollout to eu-west-gpu-pool (kernel 6.3.12 -> 6.4.1, NVIDIA 535.54 -> 535.86) we saw a cluster-wide uptick in Xid events on 2 nodes. Not a full outage but driver recoveries and one pod restart.

leo: Can you paste the dmesg/Xid lines? Also which nodes?

amanda: eu-west-gpu-12 and eu-west-gpu-19. dmesg snippet below: 
```
[12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=2345, Channel 00000000
[12345.678902] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, 00000000, 00000000
[12346.000123] nvidia: GPU has fallen off the bus: GPU 0
```

maria: gpu-monitor-bot also fired alerts: `gpu_xid_errors_total` increased from 2 -> 78 over 40m for that pool. ECC corrected counts didn't jump, but uncorrected ECC went +3 on eu-west-gpu-19.

gpu-monitor-bot: alert: eu-west-gpu-pool: gpu_xid_errors_total high (rate 1.95/min). Top nodes: eu-west-gpu-19 (47), eu-west-gpu-12 (28).

leo: Ok. First triage checklist: 
- Run `nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR` on both nodes\- Check `dmesg` for other kernel oops \- Confirm firmware version: `nvmlDeviceGetFirmwareVersion` / `nvidia-smi -q | grep Firmware`\- Run workload repro (tiny job that mimics our p99 tokenization encoder)

amanda: Ran `nvidia-smi -q` and pasted relevant bits: 
```
Product Name : NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB
Driver Version : 535.86
BAR1 Version : 3.0
GPU UUID : GPU-fa...
ECC Mode: Enabled
ECC Uncorrectable Errors: 3
```

maria: Thanks. Sounds like either the driver build + kernel ABI combo or a firmware regression on the card. We should treat this as a canary validation issue for the combined upgrade (kernel+driver+fw).

devex-jen: Proposed canary plan: 
1) Pick 3 nodes in eu-west (different racks, different host NICs) as canaries.
2) Reboot + upgrade kernel+driver stack on those 3 only (same combo that caused spike).
3) Run synthetic and production replay workload for 6 hours, watch `gpu_driver_restarts_total`, `gpu_xid_errors_total`, `node_gpu_ecc_uncorrected`, host `oom_kill` and `kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total`.
4) If no anomalies for 6h, expand to 10% of pool and run 24h soak.

leo: Rollout/rollback criteria?

maria: Abort/rollback if any of the following on canaries: 
- Xid rate > 0.5/min sustained for 10m OR > 50 in 1h
- `gpu_driver_restarts_total` increases by >=1 on any node
- `node_gpu_ecc_uncorrected` increases > 0 on any node
- Pod OOMs or kernel oops reported

amanda: Also add automated rollback hook in our deploy bot: if `gpu-monitor-bot` posts a critical alert for the canary nodes, revert driver via the package repository and reboot.

sre-oncall-bot: scheduled: canary rollout window 2026-04-02 01:00-05:00 UTC. Pager alerting enabled for critical GPU metrics.

leo: For testing, use the `gpu-stress` harness (docker image `redwood/gpu-stress:canary`) with these flags: `--p99-load 70 --duration 6h --threads 4`. Also run `nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 5` to capture utilization samples.

amanda: I ran a quick repro on eu-west-gpu-19 in a lab VM: same Xid 13 when memory alloc pattern hits a corner case. I also saw `nv_peer_mem` messages in dmesg. Suspect PCIe firmware interaction. We should collect `lspci -vvv` and `ethtool -S` for NICs in case host DMA is problematic.

maria: Good catch. Add NIC stats and pcie logs to the canary runbook. Also request OEM FW check — open a ticket with vendor referencing card serials and observed Xid codes.

devex-jen: I'll draft the runbook: steps to pick nodes, commands to collect logs, PromQL queries to monitor, and exact rollback command: 
```
# rollback driver to 535.54
apt-get install -y /pool/drivers/nvidia-535.54.deb
reboot
```

amanda: One more: capacity plan. If we need to pull nodes for replacement, we should pre-warm extra nodes in eu-west (2 spare nodes) and schedule traffic shift via `kubectl cordon + drain` with `maxUnavailable=1`.

leo: Assignments: 
- amanda: collect lspci, ethtool, complete node logs for 12 & 19 (ETA 1h)
- devex-jen: publish canary runbook + prom queries (ETA 3h)
- maria: open vendor ticket with card serials and Xid codes (ETA 2h)
- sre-oncall-bot: enable alerting and keep pager coverage during rollback window

maria: Quick question — do we want to include kernel 6.4.3 build instead of 6.4.1? Upstream had a PCIe DMA fix in 6.4.2.

leo: Good call. Add a test branch with kernel 6.4.3 + 535.86 and compare. We'll run A/B canaries (3 nodes for 6.4.1, 3 nodes for 6.4.3) to isolate kernel vs driver.

amanda: Sounds good. I'll pause any wider rollout until canaries finish.

devex-jen: I'll post the runbook link here once done. :thumbsup:

leo: Thanks team — keep updates short in this thread. If anything critical, escalate to #incidents.

sre-oncall-bot: note: created incident stub INC-2026-042 for tracking. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-042

amanda: update 1769004520 — uploaded logs tarball to /mnt/ops-share/eu-west-logs/eu-west-gpu-12-19-1769004520.tar.gz

maria: acknowledged, reviewing now.

leo: ack.
